MW2 Unlocker - quick start
==========================

1. Start the game (single player or multiplayer).
2. Double-click MW2Unlocker.exe

   - A window opens and waits for the game (up to a minute), so you can start
     it while MW2 is still loading. The status line says what it is doing.
   - If the game runs as administrator, run this program as administrator too.

3. Move the sliders, tick or untick the boxes, click the key to change it, then
   press "Apply && save".

   - If the game is already injected, the change takes effect straight away,
     the toggle key included.
   - If it is not, the value is saved and applied when the unlocker is injected.
   - The key (F6 by default) switches everything off and on again in game.

   After the game has restarted, remember to run this program again: the
   unlocker has to be injected into the new session.

The window stays open while you play and closes when the game does. Set
closeWithGame=0 in [general] to keep it open after the game exits instead.


Settings
--------
The window writes unlocker.ini next to this file, and reads it when it opens.
Editing that file in Notepad is just as valid - same settings, no sliders:

    [fps]
    value=250        frame cap. 0 = no cap at all (fastest)

    [fov]
    value=90         field of view, in degrees
    max=179          also raise the engine's own 80-degree clamp. NOT in the
                     window any more - the clamp's checkbox was taken out, so
                     this line is the only way past 80 degrees

    [music]
    enabled=0        music off. The soundtrack is streamed audio, so this switches
                     the stream off. It is kept applied while the game runs - the
                     game reloads its sound settings, so one write would not stick

    [r_fullbright] enabled=0   draw the world unlit (writes r_fullbright 1)
    [cg_draw2D]    enabled=0   hide the HUD, crosshair and counters (writes 0)
    [cg_drawGun]   enabled=0   hide the first-person weapon (writes cg_drawGun 0)
    [r_fog]        enabled=0   no distance fog (writes 0)
    [r_filmTweakEnable] enabled=0   the film colour grade ON. It is behind two
                     gates (r_filmUseTweaks and r_filmTweakEnable) and the game
                     ships both off, so this writes 1 to each

    [r_filmTweakContrast]     enabled=0  the grade's six parameters, each with a
    [r_filmTweakBrightness]   enabled=0  slider in the window. The game registers
    [r_filmTweakDesaturation] enabled=0  them at 1.4, 0, 0.2 and 1.1, 0.9, 0.7
    [r_filmTweakLightTint]    enabled=0  - the last three are the tints. A tint
    [r_filmTweakMediumTint]   enabled=0  is a *colour* cvar (red, green and blue),
    [r_filmTweakDarkTint]     enabled=0  so the same number goes into all three
                                         components: a grey tint, like the game's
                                         own

    [r_glow_allowed]          enabled=0  the bloom's four gates. The window's one
    [r_glow]                  enabled=0  "Tweak the glow" switch writes 1 to all
    [r_glowUseTweaks]         enabled=0  of them; the game ships all but r_glow
    [r_glowTweakEnable]       enabled=0  closed, so the values below do nothing
                                         until it is ticked

    [r_glowTweakRadius0]          enabled=0  the bloom itself, with a slider each.
    [r_glowTweakBloomIntensity0]  enabled=0  The engine registers them at 5, 20,
    [r_glowTweakBloomCutoff]      enabled=0  0.5 and 0; the window starts radius
    [r_glowTweakBloomDesaturation] enabled=0 and intensity lower, at 1 and 2,
                                             because 5 and 20 already wash the
                                             screen out

    [r_blur]       enabled=1   blur has no switch in the game and 0 is neutral, so
                               the window writes it whenever it saves and its
                               slider - at the foot of the glow column - is always
                               live. Confirmed working.
    [r_blacklevel] enabled=1   black level has no gate either, but its value only
                               lands at renderer set-up rather than every frame,
                               so a slider for it moved nothing visible: there is
                               no control, and this section is the only way to set
                               it. Covers -0.99 to +0.99, and negative brightens

    [cg_gun_x]     enabled=0   where the first-person weapon sits: forward.
    [cg_gun_y]     enabled=0   right (cg_gun_y) and up (cg_gun_z), in engine
    [cg_gun_z]     enabled=0   units. One switch and three sliders in the window,
                               -10.00 to +10.00

    [safeArea_adjusted_horizontal] enabled=0  the HUD safe area: the fraction of
    [safeArea_adjusted_vertical]   enabled=0  the screen the 2D overlay is laid
                                              out within, so a smaller number
                                              pulls the HUD towards the centre.
                                              Two floats registered at 1.0, with
                                              one switch and two sliders on the
                                              right of the viewmodel card. This is
                                              the pair the game's own Options menu
                                              writes

    [safeArea_horizontal]          enabled=0  the base pair of the same family,
    [safeArea_vertical]            enabled=0  registered at 0.85. NOT in the
                                              window: moving it changed nothing on
                                              screen, so its sliders were taken
                                              back out and it is set here only

    [compassSize]                  enabled=1  "Scale the compass": how large the
                                              compass strip is drawn. A float
                                              registered at 1.0 with no real
                                              ceiling (FLT_MAX is passed as the
                                              maximum), read in ten places. A HUD
                                              size, so its slider sits under the
                                              safe area's - but it has no gate of
                                              its own: its value is written
                                              whatever that switch says, and
                                              unticking the safe area leaves it
                                              alone. ! 0 crashes the game - the
                                              slider and its box floor at 0.1, and
                                              this file is not floored

    [cg_drawCrosshair]             enabled=0  "Turn on weapon crosshair", an int
                                              registered at 1 and read once as a
                                              byte gate over a block of HUD code,
                                              so 0 hides it. The window's "Hide the
                                              crosshair" switch writes that 0:
                                              enabled=1 here means hidden

    [timescale]                    enabled=0  the game's own clock, a float
                                              registered at 1.0. Below 1.0 slows
                                              the game down, above it speeds
                                              everything up; 1.0 is neutral. This
                                              and the gravity below share ONE
                                              switch in the window - the "Server"
                                              card's - and the same flag goes into
                                              both sections: with it off the cvars
                                              are handed back to the game. Slider:
                                              0.10 to 5.00. TESTING

    [phys_gravity]                 enabled=0  "Physics gravity in units/sec^2."
                                              - the gravity on objects, a float
                                              registered at 800, which is neutral;
                                              negative inverts it. Not g_gravity,
                                              which the multiplayer binary does not
                                              have. Shares the Server card's switch
                                              with the timescale, and the slider
                                              starts at -800: the same size as the
                                              engine's own with the sign flipped
                                              (range -2000 to 2000). TESTING

    [sensitivity]
    enabled=0        mouse sensitivity. NOT in the window any more: writing the
                     value was measured not to change the aim, so the slider was
                     taken out rather than left promising something that does not
                     happen. Set it here and it is written to the cvar *and* to a
                     seta sensitivity "..." line in the game's own settings file,
                     which the game reads when it starts

    [drawfps]
    enabled=0        the engine's own FPS counter - SINGLE PLAYER ONLY

    [netfps]
    enabled=0        the network fps counter - multiplayer, and not your fps

    [general] toggleKey=0x75    the in-game key: F1-F12, 0x75 is F6

The strip along the top carries the profile box: a dropdown of three slots, kept as
Profile 1.ini to Profile 3.ini in %LOCALAPPDATA%\MW2Unlocker\profiles. Choosing one
puts its settings back into the window - then press Apply & save, because choosing
one on its own changes nothing in the game. Apply & save is also what stores what
the window shows into the slot you are on, starting that file as a copy of your
config the first time. The window opens on Profile 1 and loads it if it exists, so
that is the slot to keep your everyday settings in.

The window groups music, fullbright, the HUD, the crosshair, the weapon model and
the fog - along with the in-game hotkey and "close with the game" beside it - into
one card called "Other Settings"; below that, the two testing sliders (the timescale
and the physics gravity) have a "Server" card of their own, behind a single switch
that gates both of them. The film tweak has a card of its own, laid out in two
columns - its own six sliders on the left, the glow tweak's switch and four sliders
plus the blur slider on the right - and the viewmodel card has the three offsets on
the left and the HUD safe area's two sliders with the compass under them on the
right, each column with its own switch.

Three of those cards fold away: the viewmodel, the film tweak and the Server one.
The rows do nothing while their switch is off, so they are hidden and the window
shrinks to fit - tick a switch and its rows appear right below it, untick it and
they go again. The viewmodel and film cards stay open while either of their switches
is on; the Server card has the one, so it is simply open or shut, and it starts
folded. That switch is a real gate rather than only a disclosure: with it off the
unlocker hands the timescale and the physics gravity back to the game. The switch
itself does not move, and the little triangle next to it points right while its rows
are closed and down once they are open.

The line at the very top of the window is worth reading once: some of these
settings are only picked up when a match is set up, so they do nothing until you
rejoin one. The safe area, the compass and the HUD switches are the ones that
behave that way; the frame cap, the field of view, the viewmodel and the film
tweak apply as soon as they are written.

The small dot beside the status line at the foot of the window says what the
unlocker is doing at a glance: green once the game is answering, yellow while it
is still looking for it, red if something failed. Beside the buttons is the build
number - "build 44   2026-10-02" - which is what to quote if you have a problem
with a particular build. It is stamped afresh on every build from a counter kept in
the build tree, so two builds cannot share a number. Under it is "Check for
update": it asks GitHub what the newest published build is and says so, and if
there is a newer one the next click opens the download page in your browser. It
does not download or install anything by itself.

To drop a feature entirely, put enabled=0 in its section. The two counters have no
controls in the window yet, and neither have the sensitivity or black level, so
this file is where they are switched on.


The counter on screen
---------------------
An FPS figure from the Steam overlay is not the same number as the one the game
computes for itself - the overlay counts frames that reach the GPU, the game
counts the frames its own loop produces.

The engine's own counter is available in SINGLE PLAYER only. The multiplayer
client registers the cvar and never reads it, so [drawfps] does nothing there
however you set it. In multiplayer the only counter left is [netfps], which is
the network rate rather than your frame rate.


Two things worth knowing
------------------------
* The game's own frame limiter is imprecise. It rounds your value down to a
  whole number of milliseconds, then overshoots a little, so a request of 250
  gives about 212 and a request of 167 gives about 190 (faster than asked).
  For an exact frame rate, set [fps] value=0 and cap it with your graphics
  driver (NVIDIA Control Panel -> Max Frame Rate) or RTSS instead.

* Multiplayer is VAC-protected. This is intended for single player, private
  matches and offline use. Using anything like this on a secured server can
  get your account banned.


If nothing happens
------------------
A log is written to:

    %LOCALAPPDATA%\MW2Unlocker\mw2_unlocker.log

It names the settings it found, the addresses it wrote to, and anything it
could not find.

If MW2Unlocker.exe itself disappears, Windows Defender has quarantined it - an
EXE that drops a DLL and injects it looks exactly like a loader to a heuristic
scanner. Restore it and add an exclusion for the folder. If you would rather
not, use the loose mw2_unlocker.dll + injector.exe instead; they do the same
thing without the self-extracting step.
